pages.name: The drawer, the states, the phone

artboards.title: Proposed — the Inventory console, one line open
Proposed — settled, filtered-empty, failed, and brand new

annotations.text:
THE JOB OF THIS SCREEN

I asked you four things and you answered all four. Everything on these boards follows from your answers.

1. YOU DO ALL FOUR JOBS HERE -- fix what is wrong, look one line up, read what the shelf is worth, and receive and count. So the screen cannot pick one and demote the rest. It has to order them.

2. THE SEARCH BOX LEADS. You chose it, and it is the right choice: three of the four jobs begin by naming a line. So the widest, tallest, first thing under the page name is the box you type into -- 44px, full width, above the money. Filters sit on its own row, not in a form panel above the figures.

3. 60-300 LINES. You never read the whole list, so the screen must be honest about what it is NOT showing. One line under the search says how many matched, how many are listed, and which filter is holding the rest back -- and offers it back.

4. THE MOVEMENTS LOG GETS ITS OWN DOOR. "What is on the shelf" and "how did it get that way" are different questions with different filters. Inventory keeps the last five movements in the rail with a door to all 418; the full log, with its three filters, becomes Stock movements in the rail.

5. THE PHONE ANSWERS "DO I HAVE IT?" -- drawn from scratch at 390, not reflowed. See page 2.

Everything is drawn from index.html's own values: the 23-colour palette, the 11/12/13/14/19 ramp, Inter + Archivo Black + IBM Plex Mono, and the .ow-* console components already shipping on Today, Debtors, Creditors, Consignment, Follow-ups, WhatsApp and Pricing. No new colour, no new weight, no new type size, no fourteenth button family.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT AS IT STANDS >

1. IT IS STILL A LEGACY SCREEN. .page-head, .panel, .p-toolbar, .inv-card -- radius 11 and 12 where the system is 4/6/8, a drop shadow where depth in this app is hairlines, 700 weight where the ramp says 600, 10px and 11.5px and 12.5px sizes off the ramp. Pricing, WhatsApp, Debtors, Creditors and Consignment have all moved to the console. This has not.

2. TWO CRIMSON BANNERS, 470px OF THEM, ABOVE EVERY FIGURE ON THE SCREEN. They are well written -- the best copy on the screen -- and they are there on an ordinary Tuesday when three cost records are adrift. Crimson is for the genuinely bad. Nothing here is bad; it is admin.

3. THE ROWS ARE CARDS IN FOUR COLUMNS, SO NO TWO FIGURES LINE UP. This is the one thing money must do. "1,101,600" in column one and "3,608,000" in column two cannot be compared at a glance, and comparing at a glance is the only way a stock list is ever read. Eight lines fill a 1440px screen; you have 192.

4. NOTHING RANKS. Sorted by product name, with 26 lines hidden by a default filter. The screen never says what to do first, and with 192 lines it is the only screen that could.

5. THIRTY-TWO UNLABELLED ICON BUTTONS, AND NO ACCENT ANYWHERE. Four per card. A purchase, a stock correction, a restock floor and a price-rule override are four quite different acts, and they are told apart by a 14px glyph. Meanwhile the screen's own action -- receiving a delivery -- does not exist on it at all; you reach it through one of those glyphs.

6. A TILE THAT EXISTS TO SAY NOTHING HAPPENED. "nothing left -- 0", in amber, on a healthy shelf.

7. A SECOND CONSOLE FOR A DIFFERENT QUESTION. Recent stock movements has its own search, its own category filter and its own movement filter, sitting under the first screen, sharing nothing with it.

8. AN INPUT CLIPPING ITS OWN PLACEHOLDER MID-WORD. "Track one item -- search by product, variant or n". An <input> cannot ellipsis, which is fault one of the truncation rule.

9. THE 230-CHARACTER HEADER PARAGRAPH RUNS 158 CHARACTERS A LINE, unmeasured. Six screens already put the long version behind the "i".

THE PROPOSAL -- what changed, and why

THE SEARCH IS THE SCREEN'S FIRST MOVE, and it says what it did. "166 lines listed of 192 on file - 26 are hidden because they have nothing on the shelf - show them." The old screen only told you a filter had emptied the list once the list was already empty; here it says so on every visit, so you always know what you are and are not looking at.

FIVE TILES, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS THE WHOLE SHELF -- not what the filter left. A position that shrinks because somebody left a filter on is a position nobody can trust. What the filter is worth lives in the list's own header instead: "166 lines - 18,412,600 here". The strip and the list can disagree without either of them lying, and each says which it is.

TWO CRIMSON BANNERS BECAME ONE 38px AMBER LINE with three chips, and it is GONE ENTIRELY when nothing is wrong -- not zeroed, gone. A screen that keeps a slot for problems it does not have always looks slightly broken. Opened, it is a drawer (page 2) that also states the ORDER: matching a cost record can leave new uncosted units behind it, so matching comes before pricing. The current screen relies on you fixing them in that order without saying so.

THE ROW IS 44px AND OPENS IN PLACE. Five columns, and only the name gives way -- money and counts are sized to their content, because a clipped figure is not a shortened figure, it is a wrong one. Default sort is most money tied up, so the biggest thing on your shelf is the first thing you see.

COLOUR ONLY WHERE IT MEANS SOMETHING. A count is a size, not a warning, so 88 sheets is ink. Amber where a line is under a floor you set. Crimson for nothing on this screen, because nothing on it is bad. The accent appears once: Receive a delivery.

THE OPEN LINE IS THE WHOLE OF ONE LINE'S BUSINESS -- the sentence in words, the six figures laid out so they can be checked rather than trusted, its cost-record warning with the fix on it, its last three movements, and the four acts NAMED IN WORDS instead of drawn as glyphs. Thirty-two icon buttons became four labelled ones on the line you actually opened.

THE RAIL CARRIES WHAT THE LIST CANNOT: the last five movements with a door to all 418, where the money sits by category, and when the shelf was last counted -- which is the honest caveat over every figure above it.

HEIGHT: two banners, a paragraph and a toolbar came to roughly 620px before the first figure. The search, the whole position and eight lines are now above the fold.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DECIDED FOR YOU

1. THE ACCENT IS FIXED ON "RECEIVE A DELIVERY". It could instead move to whatever the repair drawer says is most urgent. I chose the stable one: a button that moves is a button you hunt for, and receiving is the act you perform on this screen most often. Say the word and it follows the problem instead.

2. THE PHONE DOCK SAYS "COUNT IT". You said the phone job is "do I have it?" -- which is reading, not acting, and a read-only screen with no action at all felt wrong in the thumb zone. Counting is the act a person standing at the shelf actually performs, and it is the one that makes the desk figures true. If you would rather it said "Receive more" -- or nothing at all -- that is one line.

3. THE DEFAULT SORT IS "MOST MONEY TIED UP", not product name. With 192 lines and search leading, name-order buys you nothing you could not get faster by typing. If you would rather it opened least-stock-first, say so.

4. STOCK MOVEMENTS BECOMES A DOOR of its own in the rail, under Inventory. I have drawn the rail entry and the "All 418" door, but not the screen behind it -- that is its own piece of work and I did not want to design it inside this one.

5. WHAT I HAVE NOT TOUCHED: the FIFO cost arithmetic, shelfValueForKey, the consignment split, repairStockLotDrift, priceUncostedStock, the subsequence search matcher (which is very good and is now advertised in the placeholder -- "sndppr"), or any of the modals. The old names stay as search keywords: stock, shelf, count, lots.

6. THE "i" BUBBLE holds the 230-character paragraph, unchanged. I did not rewrite it, only folded it.

THE REPAIR DRAWER -- what two crimson banners became

It is a 38px amber line until you open it, and it is not there at all when there is nothing in it.

THE ORDER IS A RULE, AND IT IS SAID ON SCREEN. Matching a cost record to the shelf can leave new units with no cost behind it, so matching comes first and pricing second. The current screen depends on you doing them in that order and never mentions it.

EACH SECTION SAYS WHAT IT WILL NOT DO, as loudly as what it will. Matching changes no count, no money and no statement. Pricing records what goods already on the shelf cost. Nothing under "below their floor" orders anything until you order it.

THE THIRD SECTION IS NEW. Seven lines under their floor are today just a red pill on seven cards scattered through 192. Here they are a queue, ranked by HOW SOON EACH RUNS OUT at the rate it has actually been selling -- not by how far under it is, because two bags short of a line that sells twice a year is not a problem and four days of paint is.

AND IT NAMES WHAT IT CANNOT DO. The consigned line cannot be priced here -- pricing it would change what you owe its supplier -- so its button says where that is settled instead of failing quietly. There is no fix-all under "no cost on file", because every one of those is a figure only you know. There IS one under cost records, because there the shelf is the truth in every row and the repair is the same act done three times.

THE STATES, WHICH ARE WHERE A SCREEN IS ACTUALLY DESIGNED >

A -- NOTHING TO PUT RIGHT. No repair line, and no strip of zeros in its place. Three tiles change: the line nearest its floor, how many lines have a floor at all, and when you last counted. Those are the only readings of "nothing is wrong" worth having -- how close the shelf came to catching something, how much of it is being watched, and how old the figures are.

B -- IT MATCHED AND A FILTER HID IT. The current screen answers "No matching products", which is untrue: the product matched perfectly and a filter that is ON BY DEFAULT hid it. With Hide no stock ticked that is most of a search for something you have run out of -- the exact search where being told the thing does not exist is worst. Here it names both lines, says when you last sold one, and offers both the filter and the delivery.

C -- THE LEDGER DID NOT READ. This state does not exist today: a failed read and a clean shelf are currently indistinguishable, and only one of them is good news. The app's own law is that a failure must name itself. So it says what failed, when the last good read was, that those figures are NOT current and are not shown, and that receiving and counting are off until it reads -- because stock booked in against figures nobody can see is stock booked in blind.

D -- NO PRODUCTS YET. No strip above it. Five tiles reading 0 on a shop's first day is five figures that mean nothing and makes a new shop look like a broken app.

THE PHONE -- its own design, not the table reflowed

820px is a switch, so this is drawn from scratch at 390: 44px navy bar, 26px page name, 15-16px body, 44px+ hit targets, no fake status bar and no fake keyboard.

YOU SAID THE PHONE JOB IS "DO I HAVE IT?" -- somebody is in front of you in the yard. So search is the first and biggest thing on the screen at 52px, and the card leads with THE COUNT at 28px mono, because that is the answer to the question being asked. The money sits beside it at 15px: it is the desk's question, not the yard's.

NO METRIC STRIP. Four tiles of shillings answer a question nobody in a yard is asking, and they would cost 110px of the six inches a card list has. One line carries the whole position instead -- and it is the WHOLE shelf, not the three lines the search found, for the same reason the desk strip does not move with its filter.

THE CARDS CARRY NO BUTTON. A button on every card is a screen of accents, which is a screen with no accent. The accent lives once, in the docked navy bar in the thumb zone -- the pattern Follow-ups, Debtors, Creditors and Pricing already ship -- and it names the line most worth acting on, so the default is right without reading the list.

WHAT I DECIDED FOR YOU, and would happily undo: the dock says "Count it" rather than "Receive more". See note 2 on page 1.
